s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin condition with erythematous papules and lymphoid infiltrate
salient_findings: Erythematous papules with crusts and excoriations on the trunk and upper extremities
Scales and fissures on the lower lip with sparing of the surrounding skin
key_facts: Female patient in her early 40s
No other medical history
Topical corticosteroids did not control symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, crusts, and excoriations
Scales and fissures on the lower lip
Normal blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement
Normal urine porphyrin analysis
Skin biopsy showed spongiosis, erosions, and nodular lymphocyte infiltrate
Phototest with solar simulator showed delayed erythema to UV-A

differentials: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma
per_call: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with germinal centers and CD20 positive cells on skin biopsy

shortlist.label: Pityriasis lichenoides chronica
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous papules and scales on physical examination, consistent with chronic pruritic skin condition

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate and erythematous papules, with potential for lymphoma association

shortlist.label: Jessner's lymphocytic infiltrate
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphocytic infiltrate on skin biopsy, consistent with benign but chronic condition

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Germinal centers and CD20 positive cells on skin biopsy, with potential for follicular lymphoma

raw.rationale: The skin biopsy results showing a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center, along with CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells, are characteristic of primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma.

rejected.label: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Too broad, as primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma is a specific subtype of cutaneous B-cell lymphoma

rejected.label: Pityriasis lichenoides chronica
rejected.why: Typically presents with more superficial skin lesions and lacks the distinctive lymphoid follicles seen in this patient's biopsy

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: Characterized by a wedge-shaped infiltrate and atypical lymphocytes, which were not described in this patient's biopsy

rejected.label: Jessner's lymphocytic infiltrate
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more superficial and band-like infiltrate, and lacks the germinal centers seen in this patient's biopsy
